disclosure_text: It relates to me because my great grandfather immigrated from Spain
micronarrative: I see two sides fiercely fighting one another in ideology. I don’t connect personally or distantly; it just seems like it’s very much par for the course. This division isn’t so much a part of my real life, but rather something I encounter on the internet, especially through social media. In my hometown, political expression is mostly just graffiti or signs on people’s lawns, whereas online it’s all over the place. When I encounter those lawn signs or graffiti, I just ignore it as it’s none of my business. There are several times I’ve driven past one, but I’ve never walked past them. Being inside a car allows me to maintain that distance, unlike the vulnerability of walking past. I simply keep my head down and drive by, treating the tension as background noise rather than a personal engagement.
